mainTopic: Witnesses as judges for קידוש החודש; why the רבנן disqualify a cow's horn as a שופר; foreign words that explain words in תנ״ך
overview: The גמרא finishes a question about witnesses to the new moon: רבי עקיבא says a witness cannot become a judge, but only in דיני נפשות, where judges must look for זכות, so he agrees for קידוש החודש. A new משנה then says all שופרות are kosher except a cow's horn, because it is a קרן, and רבי יוסי objects that every שופר is called קרן. The רבנן answer that a cow's horn is never called שופר, and the two sides argue over the פסוק 'שׁוֹר פָּר'. עולא gives another reason for the רבנן: a cow's horn recalls the golden calf, and an accuser cannot become a defender. After a series of challenges about gold in the קודש הקדשים, the rule is that this applies inside, and a שופר counts as inside because it is for remembrance. אביי gives a third reason: a cow's horn is layered, so it looks like several שופרות. רבי יוסי rejects each reason. The גמרא then proves that יובל means a ram, and brings a list of words the חכמים heard in other lands that explain words in תנ״ך. The amud ends as a story about לוי begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא where רבי עקיבא says a witness cannot become a judge
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא is quoted. In it, רבי טרפון lets some of the judges act as witnesses and others as judges. רבי עקיבא says they all become witnesses, and a witness cannot become a judge. This seems to clash with our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some of them become witnesses and some of them become judges. This is רבי טרפון's view. רבי עקיבא says: they all become witnesses, and a witness cannot become a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of a ברייתא. It brought this source to show that our משנה, which lets a witness to the new moon become a judge, seems to go against רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, a whole סנהדרין saw a person commit murder. רבי טרפון says they can split up: some testify and the rest judge. רבי עקיבא forbids this, because once you are a witness you cannot be a judge, and that sounds like the opposite of our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness cannot become a judge

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the end of a quote the גמרא started just before, used to challenge our משנה about witnesses to the new moon.

phrases.english: Some of them become witnesses
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא that started just before: a סנהדרין that saw someone kill a person.

phrases.english: and some of them become judges;
these are the words of Rabbi Tarfon.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן נַעֲשִׂין עֵדִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: They all become witnesses,
and a witness cannot become a judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְצָתָן נַעֲשׂוּ עֵדִים וּמִקְצָתָן נַעֲשׂוּ דַּיָּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge the גמרא raised before this section: is our משנה against רבי עקיבא?
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה that lets someone who saw the new moon also sit as a judge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא says a witness can never become a judge, so the משנה seems to follow only רבי טרפון.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's rule applies only to capital cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can follow רבי עקיבא too. He only forbids a witness from judging in דיני נפשות, because judges there must search for reasons to save the accused. Someone who saw the murder cannot do that. For the new moon, even רבי עקיבא agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. He only said his rule there, about capital cases, because the תורה says 'the congregation shall judge' and 'the congregation shall save.' Once the judges saw him kill a person, they cannot find any merit for him. But here, even רבי עקיבא agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that רבי עקיבא's rule is limited to capital cases, so it does not clash with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דיני נפשות the תורה wants the judges to look for ways to save the accused ("והצילו העדה"). A judge who saw the killing with his own eyes cannot honestly look for זכות. Sighting the new moon has no defendant to save, so there is no reason to stop a witness from judging.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the source fits this opinion too)
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
And the congregation shall save; judges must look for ways to acquit

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's rule that a witness cannot be a judge comes from the need in דיני נפשות to look for זכות. It does not apply to witnesses for קידוש החודש.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the reason behind a rule sets its limits. Once we know why רבי עקיבא forbids it, we can see where his rule does not reach.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Akiva;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva only said his rule there
about capital cases,
since the Merciful One says: "And the congregation shall judge"
"and the congregation shall save,"
and once they have seen him kill a person
they cannot find any merit for him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא — אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מוֹדֶה.
phrases.english: But here, even Rabbi Akiva agrees.
phrases.notes: "Here" means witnesses to the new moon, the case in our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי עקיבא's opinion in the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: the rule applies only to דיני נפשות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי עקיבא forbids a witness from judging in every kind of case.
steps.terutzMaskana: His rule applies only where judges must look for זכות. For the new moon, even he lets a witness judge.

steps.title: New משנה: all horns are kosher except a cow's
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that every kind of שופר is kosher except one made from a cow's horn, because a cow's horn is called a קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All שופרות are kosher, except a cow's, because it is a קרן (a horn).
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, about the main מצוה of ראש השנה, blowing שופר. It gives the basic rule of which horns may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the default is that any animal horn works as a שופר. The one exception is a cow's horn, and the reason given is a name: it is called קרן, not שופר.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All shofars are kosher,
except for that of a cow,
because it is a "keren" (horn).

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת כְּשֵׁרִים, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unconnected to the witness discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every animal horn is a kosher שופר except a cow's, since a cow's horn is called קרן.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: every שופר is called a קרן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues against the reason in the משנה. Even a ram's horn, which is surely kosher, is called a קרן in a פסוק. So being called קרן cannot make a horn unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: But aren't all שופרות called קרן? As it says: 'When they sound a long blast with the horn (קרן) of the ram.'
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, רבי יוסי challenges the reason the תנא קמא gave for ruling out a cow's horn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says a cow's horn is unfit because it is called קרן. רבי יוסי shows from a פסוק that a ram's horn is also called קרן, so that name cannot be what makes a horn unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so...? (opens a challenge)
When they sound a long blast

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא כׇּל הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת נִקְרְאוּ קֶרֶן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: But aren't all shofars called "keren"?
As it is stated: "When they sound a long blast with the horn of the ram."
phrases.notes: יהושע 6:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason the תנא קמא gave in the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'because it is a קרן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A kosher ram's horn is also called קרן in the פסוק, so that name cannot disqualify a horn.

steps.title: The גמרא: רבי יוסי's point sounds convincing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא remarks that רבי יוסי argued well. This sets up the question: how would the רבנן answer him?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יוסי is speaking well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבי יוסי's argument looks strong. It is setting up the next step, where it explains how the רבנן answer him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By praising רבי יוסי's argument, the גמרא is really asking a question: why don't the רבנן accept it? The answer comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the discussion of the משנה
He is saying well, a good point

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Yosei is saying well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs רבי יוסי's challenge and turns it toward the רבנן
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's ruling that a cow's horn is unfit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every שופר is called קרן, the רבנן's reason seems to fall apart.

steps.title: The רבנן: a cow's horn is called only קרן, never שופר
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that other horns are called both שופר and קרן. A cow's horn is called קרן but never שופר, as the פסוק about יוסף's bull shows. So it cannot count as a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? All other horns are called שופר and are also called קרן. A cow's horn is called קרן, but it is never called שופר, as it is written: 'His firstborn bull, glory is his, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the רבנן's answer to רבי יוסי. The problem with a cow's horn is not that it is called קרן, but that it is never called שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that a ram's horn is called קרן. What matters is whether a horn is ever called שופר. Kosher horns have both names, and a cow's horn only has the name קרן, as the פסוק shows by calling a bull's horns קרנים.
steps.whatToRemember: A kosher שופר must be a horn that is called שופר. A cow's horn is only ever called קרן, so the רבנן rule it unfit.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן do not say 'anything called קרן is unfit.' They say 'anything never called שופר is unfit.' That is how they answer רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? All shofars are called "shofar"
and are also called "keren."
That of a cow is called "keren,"
but it is not called "shofar,"
as it is written: "His firstborn bull, glory is his,
phrases.notes: דברים 33:17

phrases.english: and his horns are the horns of a wild ox."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן: כׇּל הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת אִקְּרוֹ שׁוֹפָר וְאִקְּרוֹ קֶרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יוסי that the גמרא just praised
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the reason more precise: what matters is never being called שופר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the רבנן ruled out any horn called קרן, which would include a ram's horn.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a horn never called שופר is unfit. A cow's horn is called only קרן, so it is ruled out.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a cow's horn is also called a שופר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers the רבנן. A cow's horn is also called a שופר, because the words 'שׁוֹר פָּר' in a פסוק should be read together as 'מִשּׁוֹפָר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי would tell you: a cow is also called a שופר, as it says, 'And it shall please ה׳ more than an ox bull.' If it is an ox, why call it a bull? And if it is a bull, why call it an ox? Rather, what does 'ox bull' mean? 'More than a שופר.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי pushes back on the רבנן's claim (from step 6) that a cow's horn is never called a שופר. He brings a פסוק where, he says, it is called a שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two words for the same animal, שׁוֹר and פָּר, which seems repetitive. רבי יוסי says the extra wording is a hint: put the two words together and you get 'מִשּׁוֹפָר', 'than a שופר'. So a cow is called שופר too, and the רבנן's reason falls away.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei would say to you:
a cow is also called a shofar,
as it is written: "And it shall please ה׳ more than an ox bull,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 69:32

phrases.english: if it is an ox, why say bull,
and if it is a bull, why say ox?
Rather, what is "ox bull"? "More than a shofar."
phrases.notes: Read the two words מִשּׁוֹר פָּר as if they were one word: מִשּׁוֹפָר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי's reply to the רבנן's answer in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a פסוק to show the opposing claim is false
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A cow's horn is only ever called קרן, never שופר
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוסי, a cow's horn is also called שופר in תהלים

steps.title: The רבנן read the פסוק like רב מתנה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain 'שׁוֹר פָּר' differently, following רב מתנה: it means an ox as big as a bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They follow רב מתנה, for רב מתנה said: what is 'ox bull'? An ox that is as big as a bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן deal with רבי יוסי's reading, and answers that they explain the double wording in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree the two words need explaining, but they do not join them into one word. For them, the פסוק describes an ox that has grown to the size of a bull. So the פסוק never calls a cow a שופר, and their rule stands.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: how would the רבנן explain this פסוק?

phrases.english: They read it like Rav Mattana.
For Rav Mattana said:
What is "ox bull"?
That it is an ox as big as a bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רבנן's answer to רבי יוסי's proof in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offering a different reading of the same פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: It means an ox the size of a bull, so a cow is still never called שופר
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי reads 'שׁוֹר פָּר' as 'שופר'. The רבנן, following רב מתנה, read it as 'an ox as big as a bull'. So the argument about the cow's horn comes down to how to read this פסוק.

steps.title: עולא: a prosecutor cannot become a defender
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives a different reason for the רבנן, based on רב חסדא: the כהן גדול does not wear gold in the קודש הקדשים, because something that accuses cannot defend.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: this is the reason of the רבנן, like רב חסדא. For רב חסדא said: why does the כהן גדול not go into the innermost room in his gold clothes to do the service? Because a prosecutor cannot become a defender.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא offers a completely new reason why the רבנן disqualify a cow's horn. It has nothing to do with the name שופר or קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול enters the קודש הקדשים in white clothes, not gold, because gold would recall the sin of the golden calf. Something that 'accuses' the Jewish people cannot be used to 'defend' them. In the same way, a cow's horn recalls the calf, so it cannot be used for the שופר, which is meant to bring us merit.

keyTerms.meaning: the golden garments of the כהן גדול
the innermost place, the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Ulla said:
This is the reason of the Rabbis,
like Rav Chisda.
For Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל נִכְנָס
phrases.english: Why does the High Priest not enter
in golden garments into the innermost place
to do the service?
Because a prosecutor cannot become a defender.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the argument over the פסוק and offers a new reason for the רבנן's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cow's horn is not kosher because it recalls the golden calf, and an accuser cannot act as a defender
steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not continuing the argument about the words שופר and קרן. He gives a totally separate reason for the same ruling in the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that something tied to a sin cannot be used to ask for forgiveness, explains both the כהן גדול's white clothes on יום כיפור and the rule against a cow's horn.

steps.title: But the bull's blood is brought inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's rule: on יום כיפור the blood of a bull is brought into the קודש הקדשים, even though a bull recalls the calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it not so? But there is the blood of the bull!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule that nothing recalling the calf may be used in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a cow is an 'accuser' because of the golden calf, the bull of יום כיפור should be a problem too. Yet its blood is sprinkled right inside the קודש הקדשים. This seems to go against רב חסדא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: the blood of the bull brought on יום כיפור

phrases.english: And is it not so?
phrases.notes: He means: do we really never bring anything from a cow into the קודש הקדשים?

phrases.english: But there is the blood of the bull!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's rule quoted by עולא
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that an accuser cannot be a defender
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bull's blood recalls the calf, yet it is brought into the קודש הקדשים, which seems to contradict the rule

steps.title: Blood is different because it has changed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the blood is not the animal itself. Since it has changed form, it does not recall the calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it has changed, it has changed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge about the bull's blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is no longer the bull itself; it has changed form. So it does not bring the golden calf to mind and is not an 'accuser'. A cow's horn, however, still looks like part of the animal, so the rule applies to it.

phrases.english: Since it has changed, it has changed.
phrases.notes: He means: blood is no longer the bull itself, so it does not remind anyone of the calf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the bull's blood in step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: changed form versus the original thing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything from a cow recalls the calf and cannot be brought inside
steps.terutzMaskana: Only something that is still recognizably the animal recalls the calf; blood has changed, so it is fine
steps.whatToRemember: עולא's reason: a cow's horn recalls the golden calf, and an accuser cannot be a defender. The bull's blood on יום כיפור is not a problem because it has changed form.

steps.title: But the Ark, its cover and the cherubs are gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's rule: the ארון, כפורת and כרובים are covered in gold, yet they stand inside the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the Ark, the Ark cover and the cherub, which are gold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule that gold, which recalls the golden calf, may not be in the קודש הקדשים. Gold objects are permanently there!
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gold 'accuses' just by being in the קודש הקדשים, the ארון and כפורת should be a problem. Since they clearly belong there, the rule as stated seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: The Ark, which held the Tablets
The gold cover on top of the Ark
Cherub, the gold figures on the כפורת

phrases.english: But there are the Ark, the Ark cover and the cherub!
phrases.notes: All of these are gold, and they sit inside the קודש הקדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the bull's blood question was answered, a new challenge comes from gold objects in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that gold may not enter the קודש הקדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gold objects stand in the קודש הקדשים all the time, so gold being there cannot be forbidden.

steps.title: The rule is only about what a sinner brings in
steps.stepSummary: The rule is only that a sinner should not bring gold in when he comes for atonement. Objects already there are not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are saying that a sinner should not bring gold in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule. It only forbids a sinner from bringing gold in to ask for atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון and כפורת are not brought in by the כהן גדול as part of asking for forgiveness. The problem is only gold that the sinner himself brings in.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner, here the one asking for atonement
Should not bring near / bring in

phrases.english: We are saying that a sinner should not bring [gold] in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gold in the קודש הקדשים is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only gold the sinner brings in is a problem.

steps.title: But the spoon and coal pan are gold and brought in
steps.stepSummary: The gold spoon and coal pan are brought into the קודש הקדשים on יום כיפור, so the narrowed rule still seems broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the spoon and the coal pan!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the narrowed rule. The כהן גדול does bring gold items in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spoon and coal pan for the incense are gold, and the כהן גדול carries them in himself. So even 'a sinner should not bring gold in' does not hold.

phrases.english: But there are the spoon and the coal pan!
phrases.notes: These are gold, and the כהן גדול carries them in for the incense on יום כיפור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'a sinner should not bring gold in'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן גדול brings the gold spoon and coal pan in himself.

steps.title: The rule is only about wearing gold
steps.stepSummary: The rule is that a sinner should not adorn himself with gold. Carrying gold tools is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are saying that a sinner should not adorn himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule again. It is about dressing up in gold, not carrying gold tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spoon and coal pan are tools for the service, not decorations on the person. The problem is a sinner beautifying himself with gold while asking for forgiveness.

phrases.english: We are saying that a sinner should not adorn himself [with gold].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gold the sinner brings in is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only gold the sinner wears as decoration is a problem.

steps.title: But he wears gold clothes outside
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול wears his gold clothes outside the קודש הקדשים, even on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the gold garments worn outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the newest version of the rule. The כהן גדול does adorn himself with gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בגדי זהב are worn during the outside service. If a sinner may never adorn himself with gold, these should be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold garments of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: But there are the gold garments worn outside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'a sinner should not adorn himself with gold'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן גדול does wear gold clothes, outside.

steps.title: The rule is only inside
steps.stepSummary: The rule against wearing gold applies only inside the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule is only for inside the קודש הקדשים. Outside, gold clothes are fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the rule has its final shape: a sinner should not wear gold inside the קודש הקדשים. This sets up the next question about a שופר.

phrases.english: We are speaking about inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to a place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wearing gold anywhere is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only wearing gold inside the קודש הקדשים is a problem.

steps.title: But a שופר is blown outside too
steps.stepSummary: If the rule is only inside, it should not apply to a שופר, which is never blown in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A שופר is also outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the new limit against the case at hand. A שופר is blown outside, so why should a cow's horn be a problem?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The narrowing in step 17 saved the rule but now seems to undo the whole reason for the רבנן. A cow's horn recalls the calf, but if it is used outside, the rule should not apply.

phrases.english: A שופר is also outside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 17 to challenge עולא's reason for the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's reason for disqualifying a cow's horn
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is only inside, and a שופר is blown outside.

steps.title: A שופר is for remembrance, so it counts as inside
steps.stepSummary: Since the שופר is blown so that we are remembered before הקב״ה, it is treated as if it were inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is for remembrance, it is like inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the שופר is special. Its purpose is remembrance, so it counts as inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the קודש הקדשים the כהן גדול stands before הקב״ה to ask for mercy. The שופר does the same job of bringing us to be remembered, so the same rule applies.
steps.whatToRemember: The final rule: something that recalls the calf may not be used inside the קודש הקדשים, and a שופר counts as inside because it is for remembrance. So according to עולא, the רבנן rule a cow's horn unfit for שופר.

phrases.english: Since it is for remembrance —
it is considered like inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Treating one case like another because they share a purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שופר is outside, so the rule does not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שופר is for remembrance, so it is treated as inside.

steps.title: But the תנא said the reason is 'it is a קרן'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא gave the reason as 'because it is a קרן', not because of the calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא said 'because it is a horn'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא from the text itself. The תנא gave a different reason for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן disqualify a cow's horn because it is called a קרן and not a שופר. That is a reason about its name, not about recalling the calf, so עולא's reason seems not to be the תנא's.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn, a name different from שופר

phrases.english: But the תנא said, 'because it is a horn'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא קֶרֶן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the gold questions and challenges עולא's reason from the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנא gave a different reason: the name קרן.

steps.title: The תנא gave two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The תנא gave one reason and then another: an accuser cannot become a defender, and also it is called a קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gave one reason and another: one, that an accuser cannot become a defender; and another, that it is a horn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both reasons are true. The תנא said 'it is a קרן' as an extra reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no conflict between עולא and the תנא. The main idea is קטיגור and סניגור, and the name קרן is added as a second reason.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, a cow's horn is not kosher for שופר for two reasons: it recalls the golden calf (an accuser cannot defend), and it is called a קרן, not a שופר.

phrases.english: He said one reason and another:
One — that an accuser cannot become a defender,
and another — because it is a horn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Because it is a קרן' is the only reason, so it replaces עולא's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a second reason, added to 'an accuser cannot become a defender'.

steps.title: How would רבי יוסי answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי, who allows a cow's horn, would answer the reasons just given for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי, how would he answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks how רבי יוסי would deal with the arguments it just gave for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9-21 built a strong case for the רבנן: the calf reason and the 'it is a קרן' reason. Since רבי יוסי allows a cow's horn, he must have an answer to both.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei?
phrases.notes: Short for: how would רבי יוסי answer the reasons we just gave for the רבנן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending the רבנן to asking how the other side responds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יוסי deals with the calf reason and the 'קרן' reason.

steps.title: רבי יוסי rejects both reasons
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that the 'accuser' rule applies only inside, and a שופר is blown outside. Also, every שופר is called a קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: What you said, that an accuser cannot become a defender, applies only inside, and a שופר is blown outside. And what you said, 'because it is a קרן', every שופר is also called a קרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי's answer to both reasons for the רבנן, one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 the רבנן treated the שופר 'as if inside' because it brings us to be remembered before הקב״ה. רבי יוסי does not accept that, so for him the שופר is simply outside and the calf problem does not apply. The name 'קרן' proves nothing, because a kosher ram's horn is also called a קרן, as his פסוק in the משנה showed.

keyTerms.meaning: Accuser, prosecutor (here, a reminder of the golden calf)

phrases.english: He would say to you:
That which you said,
an accuser cannot become a defender
this applies only inside,
and this shofar is outside.
And what you said, because it is a keren,
all shofaros are also called keren.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The calf rule applies only inside and a שופר is blown outside. All שופרות are called קרן, so the name proves nothing.

steps.title: אביי's reason: one shofar, not several
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the רבנן disqualify a cow's horn because the תורה requires one שופר, and a layered cow's horn looks like two or three.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is the reason of the רבנן. The תורה said 'a שופר', not two or three שופרות. A cow's horn is made of layer upon layer, so it looks like two or three שופרות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a completely new reason for the רבנן that has nothing to do with the golden calf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reason was about the calf (an accuser). אביי instead points to how the horn looks: the תורה asks for a single שופר, and a cow's horn, built in layers, looks like several horns stacked together.

phrases.english: Abaye said,
this is the reason of the Rabbis:
The Merciful One said "a shofar,"
and not two or three shofaros.
And this one of a cow,
since it stands in layers upon layers,
it looks like two or three shofaros.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reason for the רבנן instead of the calf reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cow's horn is disqualified because its layers make it look like several שופרות, and the תורה requires one.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'because it is a קרן'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: the תנא gave the reason 'because it is a קרן', not the layers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא said 'because it is a קרן'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's reason by pointing to the reason written in the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the real reason were the layers, why does the משנה give the name 'קרן' as the reason? This is the same kind of challenge that was raised against the calf reason in step 20.

phrases.english: But the tanna
said "because it is a keren"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא קֶרֶן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reason from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reason (the layers look like several שופרות)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives a different reason, the name 'קרן', so אביי's reason seems to go against the text.

steps.title: The תנא gave two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The תנא meant two reasons: first, the תורה requires one שופר, not several, and also, it is called a קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said one reason and another. One: the תורה said one שופר, not two or three שופרות. And another: because it is a קרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's reason is an extra reason, and אביי's reason stands alongside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same answer the גמרא gave for the calf reason in step 21. The name 'קרן' does not cancel אביי's reason; it is just one of two reasons, and אביי's layers reason is the first.

keyTerms.meaning: One reason, and another one too

phrases.english: He said one reason and another:
One: that the Merciful One said one shofar,
and not two or three shofaros.
And another: because it is a keren.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה as giving two reasons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's only reason is the name 'קרן', which leaves no room for אביי's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא gave אביי's reason first and then added 'it is a קרן'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the layers are joined, so it is one שופר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that the layers of a cow's horn are attached to each other, so it counts as one שופר, and every שופר is called a קרן anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי would say to you: What you said, 'the תורה said one שופר, not two or three', is no problem. Since the layers are attached to each other, it is one. And what you said, 'because it is a קרן', every שופר is also called a קרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוסי would push back on both reasons given for the רבנן: אביי's 'one שופר' reason and the משנה's 'it is a קרן' reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן look at how the horn appears, layered like several horns. רבי יוסי looks at how it is built: the layers are joined together, so it is truly one horn. The 'קרן' reason fails for the same reason as before.
steps.whatToRemember: The two sides read the cow's horn differently. For the רבנן it is disqualified (as a reminder of the calf, or because its layers look like several שופרות). For רבי יוסי it is kosher: it is blown outside, its layers are joined into one horn, and every שופר is called a קרן.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei would say to you:
What you said, "The Merciful One said one shofar,
and not two or three shofaros"
since they are attached to each other, it is one.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the layers of the cow's horn.

phrases.english: And what you said, "because it is a keren"
all shofaros are also called keren.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי's reply to אביי's two-reason version of the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both reasons in אביי's version: the 'one שופר' reason and the 'קרן' reason.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Joined layers make one horn, not several, and the name 'קרן' applies to every שופר.

steps.title: How do we know יובל means a ram?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the word יובל means a ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that this word 'יובל' means a ram?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that 'יובל' in רבי יוסי's proof means a ram. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי proved from 'קרן היובל' that a ram's horn is called a קרן. That proof only works if יובל really means a ram, so the גמרא asks for evidence.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it implied? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where is it implied
that this word 'yovel'
phrases.notes: This is the word from רבי יוסי's פסוק in the משנה, 'קרן היובל.'

phrases.english: is a word for a ram?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the word יובל in רבי יוסי's proof from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Evidence that יובל means a ram.

steps.title: In Arabia they called a ram יובלא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבי עקיבא heard people in Arabia call a ram 'יובלא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא said, 'When I went to Arabia, they called a ram יובלא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא reports that in Arabia a ram was called 'יובלא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arabic is a related language, so the word people used there shows what the same word in the פסוק means. This supports רבי יוסי's proof that a ram's horn is called a קרן.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Akiva said:
When I went to Arabia,
they called a ram 'yovla.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The everyday language of Arabia shows that יובל means a ram.
steps.whyThisMatters: This report opens a list of similar travel reports that the גמרא brings next.

steps.title: In Galia a נדה was called גלמודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא heard a נדה called 'גלמודה' and explains it as 'this one is cut off from her husband.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא also said: 'When I went to Galia, they called a נדה גלמודה.' What does גלמודה mean? This one (דא) is cut off (גמולה) from her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a related travel report from רבי עקיבא. It is about the word 'גלמודה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is split into two parts, גמולה + דא, meaning 'this one is separated.' A נדה is separated from her husband, so the word fits.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her monthly period, separated from her husband

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva said:
When I went to Galia,
they called a נדה 'galmuda.'
What does 'galmuda' mean?
This one is cut off from her husband.
phrases.notes: The word is being split into two parts: גמולה (cut off) and דא (this one).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another travel report from the same רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גלמודה means a woman separated from her husband, like a נדה.

steps.title: In Africa a מעה was called קשיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא heard people in Africa call a מעה coin 'קשיטה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא also said: 'When I went to Africa, they called a מעה קשיטה.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third travel report from רבי עקיבא, this time about the name of a coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מעה is a small coin. In Africa people called it 'קשיטה'. The next steps explain why this is useful to know.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin, the same as a מעה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva said:
When I went to Africa,
they called a ma'ah 'kesita.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רבי עקיבא's reports.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קשיטה is a name for a מעה coin.

steps.title: Why does knowing about קשיטה matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what we gain from knowing that a קשיטה is a מעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this fact about a coin matters. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of this list is to explain words in the תורה. So the גמרא wants to know which פסוק this word helps us understand.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why step 31 matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which text the word קשיטה helps explain.

steps.title: It explains 'one hundred קשיטה' in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: Knowing this explains the 'one hundred קשיטה' that יעקב paid in the תורה: it means one hundred coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed to explain 'one hundred קשיטה' in the תורה: one hundred דנקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this explains the price יעקב paid for his field: one hundred small coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this report, we would not know what a קשיטה is. Now we know that יעקב paid one hundred מעה coins, also called דנקי.

keyTerms.meaning: Small coins, another name for מעות

phrases.english: To explain 'one hundred kesita' in the תורה,
phrases.notes: בראשית 33:19

phrases.english: which means one hundred dankei coins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It tells us the price in בראשית 33:19 was one hundred מעות.

steps.title: In the sea towns a sale was called כירה
steps.stepSummary: רבי reports that in the sea towns people called a sale 'כירה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: 'When I went to the sea towns, they called a sale כירה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar travel report from a different חכם, רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word means a sale, not digging. The next steps show which פסוק this explains.

keyTerms.meaning: A sale, in the local language

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: When I went to the sea towns,
they called a sale 'kirah.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a report from רבי in the same style as רבי עקיבא's reports.

steps.title: Why does knowing about כירה matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks what difference this fact makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question is asked again, this time about the word כירה. It sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like with קשיטה, the גמרא wants to know which פסוק this word helps explain.

phrases.english: What difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why step 34 matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק the word כירה helps explain.

steps.title: It explains 'אשר כריתי לי'
steps.stepSummary: The fact helps explain יעקב's words 'which I bought for myself' about his burial place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed to explain 'אשר כריתי לי': which I bought for myself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this explains the word כריתי in יעקב's words about his grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כריתי could be read as 'I dug.' The local word shows it can also mean 'I bought.' So יעקב is saying he bought the grave.

phrases.english: To explain 'which I karisi for myself.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:5. Because of רבי's report, read it as 'which I bought.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 35.

steps.title: A bride is called נינפי and a rooster שכוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש reports that in קן נשריא people called a bride 'נינפי' and a rooster 'שכוי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: 'When I went to the district of קן נשריא, they called a bride נינפי and a rooster שכוי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more travel report, from רבי שמעון בן לקיש. It contains two words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two new words: נינפי (bride) and שכוי (rooster). The next steps give the פסוק that each word helps explain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
When I went to the district of Kan Nishrayya,
they called a bride 'ninfi,'
and a rooster 'sekhvi.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: כְּשֶׁהָלַכְתִּי לִתְחוּם קַן נִשְׁרַיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another travel report in the same series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נינפי means a bride and שכוי means a rooster.

steps.title: The פסוק for נינפי: 'יפה נוף'
steps.stepSummary: The word נוף in 'יפה נוף משוש כל הארץ' is linked to נינפי, a bride.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bride is called נינפי. Which פסוק does this explain? 'Beautiful נוף, the joy of the whole earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which פסוק the word נינפי helps explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נוף sounds like נינפי. So 'יפה נוף' means as beautiful as a bride, the joy of the whole land.

keyTerms.meaning: Linked here to נינפי, a bride

phrases.english: A bride is called 'ninfi':
which פסוק does it explain?
'Beautiful nof, the joy of the whole earth.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 48:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first word from step 37.
steps.raayaObject: That the word נינפי helps explain a פסוק.

steps.title: The פסוק for שכוי: the rooster's understanding
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in איוב 'who gave understanding to the שכוי' is about the rooster. The 'hidden parts' in the same פסוק are the kidneys.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rooster is called שכוי. רב יהודה said in the name of רב, or some say רבי יהושע בן לוי: Which פסוק does this explain? 'Who put wisdom in the hidden parts, or who gave understanding to the שכוי?' 'Who put wisdom in the hidden parts' means the kidneys. 'Who gave understanding to the שכוי' means the rooster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which פסוק the word שכוי helps explain, and it reads both halves of that פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thanks to the local word, we know that שכוי in איוב means a rooster. The first half of the פסוק, טוחות, is explained as the kidneys. There is a doubt about who said this: רב, or רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you prefer, say (some give a different name for who said it)

steps.whatToRemember: This whole section shows that the חכמים used the everyday language of other places to explain hard words in תנ״ך: יובל, גלמודה, קשיטה, כריתי, נוף, and שכוי.

steps.title: לוי arrives in a town and a man approaches him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story about לוי visiting a certain place, where a man comes before him to speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי happened to come to a certain place. A man came before him and said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new story about לוי, and this line only sets the scene. It is getting ready for the man's words, which come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 37-39 showed rare words being explained by how people spoke in a certain place. This story follows the same pattern: someone uses a local word in front of לוי. Here we only hear who was there and that the man spoke. What he said comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come, arrived by chance

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the run of stories that explain unusual words from how people spoke in a particular place, begun with ריש לקיש's report in step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a story: לוי visits a place and a man comes to speak to him. His words will show a local word meaning.
